<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s).

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/deployment/environment-variables.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/adding-a-metadata-type.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via SchemaRegistry (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9009270cc1082a12bb519a8d5bb8739e38c238bb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ee5f03e29b92638caddeccd2e22828a021013d6c` — the merge of head `075fb3188b5aec8cd9d572ef7f48516562ce23cb` into base `9009270cc1082a12bb519a8d5bb8739e38c238bb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ee5f03e29b92638caddeccd2e22828a021013d6c && git checkout ee5f03e29b92638caddeccd2e22828a021013d6c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9009270cc1082a12bb519a8d5bb8739e38c238bb 075fb3188b5aec8cd9d572ef7f48516562ce23cb && git checkout -B drift-repro 9009270cc1082a12bb519a8d5bb8739e38c238bb && git merge --no-ff 075fb3188b5aec8cd9d572ef7f48516562ce23cb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9009270cc1082a12bb519a8d5bb8739e38c238bb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9009270cc1082a12bb519a8d5bb8739e38c238bb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Epic red-line read at `ed0f2baa` · 2026-11-12T04:42Z

Head-sha: `ed0f2baa0d5ad4212ce73920ea2ec5670f731369`

Base: merge-base `9009270cc1`. Read: the full diff (3 files, +228/−3): `registry.ts` (`pairRowBinding`, `declaredOverrideBase`), the changeset, and the 9 new pins in `package-scoped-resolver.test.ts`. Static read; nothing was run. Applies the seat's pre-PR ruling to server seat 5 (the widening is a corrected false 409, admitted only with a genuine two-holder CONTROL).

**PASS on the three red lines.**

- **Red line 1 (resolution never loosened).** The one widening is the bare read of a name held by one package of an App, beside a row of the App's pair. It moves 409 → served. That 409 came from `overlaySlotBinding` counting the shared pair as a third holder. Counting holders the way the exact read does (`isPairOf`, `pairRowOnAddress`) restores red line 3's unique-holder answer; it is not a loosening.
  - The condition is met: `CONTROL — two real holders (two independent Apps, no shared pair) still refuse the bare read naming both, with or without a pair row beside them`.
  - With two packages of the App holding the name, the bare read and `?package=A` still answer 409, now naming the two packages.
- **Red line 2 (ambiguity reported, never guessed).** `pairRowBinding` binds in this order:
  - to a declared holder only when the pair customizes it;
  - else to the App whose own pair it is;
  - else to the single owner;
  - else to no package (`undefined`).

  A declared package that holds nothing binds to no package. Nothing picks between candidates. A row no holder's pair stores keeps the per-package reading (`NOT_A_PAIR_ROW_OF_A_HOLDER`).
- **Red line 3 (independently releasable).** No schema or row change; the ADR-0087 `not-required` marker is present.
  - Every moved reader is declared FROM → TO in the changeset under `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: `packageScopedHoldersOf`, `getPackageScopedItem`, `bundleMembersHeldBy`, the undeclared-holder row, and `?package=A`. `getEnvironmentScopedItem` is declared unchanged.
  - Each move is pinned with its BASE in the title. The #28390 ruling A CONTROL is kept.

Landing note: `registry.ts` is shared with `du44hj` (#32513) and `phk4r9` (#32497). Trial-merge before queueing; it lands after #32497.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ed0f2baa0d5ad4212ce73920ea2ec5670f731369`
Local-runs: none
Scope: (no `hits` — narrowing face, no schema and no governed path) + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts

Read for this record: card #32408 (body and its 4 comments: 6792808340, 6812609395, 6813452518, 6814725254), the PR body, the 3-file list, the net diff against `main`, and the head's check-runs. The cited code was read at the head, outside the diff: `pairRowOnAddress`, `pairMemberOwners`, `isAppPairOf`, `exactQualifierItem` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`) and `appOf`, `pairOf`, `pairsOf`, `isPairOf` (`packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts`). The test file and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; they were read only to judge `registry.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

Every move follows from one change: `overlaySlotBinding` asks `pairRowBinding` before the per-package reading, when some composite holder is a package the row's pair customizes.

- **Bare-name gate, sealed (PR table row 1) — narrowing, right.** A pair row declaring X is no longer the App's bundle member, so a later package carrying only that locale is an addition to the App's template and is refused naming the App. This makes the #28802 addition rule real: the App never shipped that locale, the row is X's. It takes no declared capability away.
- **`packageScopedHoldersOf` (row 2) — right.** The pair leaves the holder set when the App holds no item of the name. A pair is a customization store, never a holder (ADR-0146 D3).
- **Bare read, one package of the App holding (row 3) — widening, right as a corrected false refusal.** The 409 named X and X's own customization store as two holders. Read in the code: two genuine holders still refuse. Two packages of one App both holding give `owners.length === 2`, the row binds to no package, and both stay in the holder set. Two independent Apps each stay a composite holder, whatever the pair row binds to. Both controls are pinned in the harness.
- **Refusal candidates, two packages of the App holding (row 4) — right.** X and Y, without the pair.
- **`getPackageScopedItem(X)` and `getPackageScopedItem(pair)` (rows 5, 6) — right.** They now agree with what `?package=X` serves; the pair's own address is served by the protocol, not by this reader.
- **`bundleMembersHeldBy` (row 7) — right.** It feeds row 1.
- **Row declaring a non-holder (row 8) — right.** It binds to no package, matching `pairRowOnAddress` answering `not-member` on every address. Fail-closed for off-door data.
- **`getEnvironmentScopedItem` (row 9) — unchanged, right.** `pairRowBinding` never answers `null`.
- **Legacy per-package pair — unchanged, right.** `owners` is empty when the legacy pair is not installed, and the per-package reading follows. When installed and the base is its own unit, the App arm or the one-owner arm answers the same base.
- **Not derived by the PR — see ④ F1.** A bundled name held by one package of the App plus a bundle addition from another package of the same App.

No public export, signature or schema changes. `pairRowBinding`, `declaredOverrideBase` and the sentinel are module-private.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: a kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves. Correct.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body, and the two agree. It matches the claim amendment 6813452518. One narrowing is published, and it is the one declared.
- The BREAKING banner, the FROM/TO list per reader, the one-line fix ("ship a locale the App ships too, or rename the template") and the ADR-0087 `not-required` disposition are present. No stored row changes shape, so the disposition holds.
- The widening is stated in the changeset body under `packageScopedHoldersOf`. The declaration line carries one arm by rule, and the narrowing arm is the binding one.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in report 6814725254. Nothing to answer.
- **Escalated to the lane seat — the epic ruling is not on the card.** The PR body and the report cite "epic seat 1" as having ruled that the three moves stay and that the widening is compliant. The card thread holds no comment from the epic seat: its newest statement on the point is the amendment 6813452518, "the epic seat's red-line read of both is pending". This record judged the widening on the code (① row 3) and does not stand in for that read. The claim 6812609395 says the read is owed by `epic:#31527#1` before ACCEPT; the lane seat confirms it exists where it was posted.
- Deviation, surface (`registry.ts`, not `packages/metadata`): covered by the amendment. Accepted.
- Deviation, `getPackageScopedItem` and `packageScopedHoldersOf` move with the two named readers: this is the consequence of fixing the one binding, each move is declared, and ① judges each. Accepted.
- Deviation, commit-card trailers of #32214's history: outside the contract scope; lane seat's.
- Out-of-scope note, a row declaring a non-owner is off-door data: agreed, and its new binding is fail-closed. No carrier needed.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, read sentence by sentence against `pairRowOnAddress`.

Agreement holds on: declaration read first; the App arm (`appOf(holder) === holder` and `pairOf(holder).value === pairId` is `isAppPairOf` exactly); one owner; two or more owners; the sentinel fall-through. The registry does not import `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, as the body says.

- **F1 — should-fix. The binding and the exact read count owners over different holder sets, and they disagree for a bundled name with an addition.** `pairRowBinding` filters `composite` (`compositeHoldersOf`: every package with a composite slot). The exact read passes `registry.packageScopedHoldersOf(type, name)`, which drops a bundle addition (#28802: "a bundle ADDITION holds no name"). Scenario, read in the code and not run: `email_template` `welcome`; X of App A ships `en-US`; Y of App A, depending on X, adds `fr-FR`; the App holds nothing; `A.custom` stores an undeclared `de-DE` row.
  - Exact read at `?package=X`: holders are `[X]` (Y is an addition), one owner, a base of the address: `serve`.
  - Registry: `owners` is `[X, Y]`, so the row binds to no package. `getPackageScopedItem(X, 'de-DE')` misses it, `bundleMembersHeldBy(X)` does not count it, and the bare read resolves to X without it.
  
  This contradicts the jsdoc ("every reader ... answers the owner the exact address serves it to") and the changeset ("else the one package of the App holding the name"), since an addition holds no name by the registry's own rule. It is not a regression: before this PR the row bound to the pair itself. It errs on the refusing side, and never picks a wrong package. The fix is either to count owners over holders that are not bundle additions, or to declare the deviation in the jsdoc and the changeset and pin it. Either earns a delta review.
- **F2 — nit.** `pairRowBinding` calls `pairOf(holder, installed)` twice and reads `.value` through a cast. One call narrowed on `.ok` reads the same. No effect on the answer.
- **F3 — nit.** `pairRowDeclaresAnotherHolder` in `getPackageScopedItem` is now reachable only for a pair that customizes no holder. Its jsdoc on `getPackageScopedItem` still describes the App's shared pair, which `pairRowBinding` now answers first. Prose only.

**Gate verdicts on this head** (48 check-runs): 15 concluded `success`, 16 `skipped`, 17 not concluded when this record was written. No failure. Concluded green: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Plan Test Core shards, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, filter. Not concluded: Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus. This verdict is the contract's; it does not cover those 17, and a red one among them stands on its own.

## Epic red-line read, delta at `d9d3621f` · 2026-11-12T04:51Z

Head-sha: `d9d3621f0e100d62cf5d2dd6afc69ca6aee52762`

Scope: `ed0f2baa..d9d3621f`, over the PASS 6814761042. Read: `pairRowBinding` and the new `ownersHoldingAName`, the changeset line, and the new pins in `package-scoped-resolver.test.ts` and `package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts`. Static read; nothing was run.

**PASS on the three red lines.**

- **Red line 1 (resolution never loosened).** The undeclared arm now counts owners the way the exact read counts holders: a bundle addition is no second owner. The one exception is an addition that ships the row's own member; it stays an owner. This brings the registry's answer in line with `?package=X` on the counter-example, and it widens nothing beyond the declared rows.
- **Red line 2 (ambiguity reported, never guessed).** When an addition ships the row's member, the row could customize either package's member, and the registry binds it to no package. That shape is pinned as a CONTROL.
- **Residual, which this PR does not introduce.** For that same shape, the exact read on `main` still serves the row at `?package=X`. The divergence is filed as #32561, with the epic seat's direction: the exact read adopts the registry's conservative count. It is declared in the PR body. It does not block this PR, because the registry side is the one that does not guess.
- **Red line 3 (independently releasable).** The changeset is updated, and the moved answers stay declared and pinned as at 6814761042.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `d9d3621f0e100d62cf5d2dd6afc69ca6aee52762`
Local-runs: none
Scope: (no `hits` — narrowing face, no schema and no governed path) + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts

This is the delta round on record 6814798935 (head `ed0f2baa0d5ad4212ce73920ea2ec5670f731369`). It covers that record's findings F1, F2 and F3 and the diff `ed0f2baa..d9d3621f`: one commit, 4 files, +94/−15. Read at the head, outside the diff: `packageScopedHoldersOf`, `bundleMembersHeldBy`, `isBundleAddition`, `collectBundle` (`registry.ts`), `pairRowOnAddress`, `pairMemberOwners` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-exact-qualifier.ts`) and `appOf` (`packages/metadata-core/src/customization-pair-lookup.ts`). The two test files and the changeset are the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`; they were read only to judge `registry.ts`.

**Earlier findings**

- **F1 — closed under the seat ruling.** `pairRowBinding` now passes its owners through `ownersHoldingAName`, which drops an owner whose holding is a bundle addition to another owner's bundle (`isBundleAddition`, the rule `packageScopedHoldersOf` applies). The counter-example was traced in the code: X ships `en-US`, Z of the same App depends on X and adds `fr-FR`, the pair stores an undeclared `de-DE` row. Owners are X and Z, Z is an addition, the row binds to X. `packageScopedHoldersOf` answers X alone, so `?package=X` serves the row too. The two agree.
- **The pin is real.** Two cases pin it: `unbound, beside a bundle addition of another package of the App` (`package-scoped-resolver.test.ts`) and `[#32408, contract review F1]` (`package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts`). At `ed0f2baa` the row bound to no package (two owners), so `getPackageScopedItem(X, 'de-DE')` answered nothing and both assertions on the registry would be red. Not run; read.
- **F2 — closed.** One `pairOf` call, narrowed on `.ok`, no cast.
- **F3 — closed.** The jsdoc on `getPackageScopedItem` now says `pairRowBinding` answers a row of the App's pair first, and `pairRowDeclaresAnotherHolder` covers a pair that customizes none of the holders.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Undeclared pair row, bundled name, one owner plus additions of the same App — right.** FROM no package (at `ed0f2baa`; the pair's own item on `main`) TO the one package holding the name. This is the F1 ruling.
- **Undeclared pair row whose locale an addition itself ships — no package; accepted by the seat, not graded.** Traced: Z ships `fr-FR`, the row is `fr-FR`, Z stays an owner, two owners, no package. `packageScopedHoldersOf` still answers X alone, so `?package=X` serves the row while the registry binds it to nobody. The seat ruled this the conservative answer (report, never guess) and is reporting it to the epic seat. The CONTROL pin exists: `CONTROL — unbound, of the very locale a bundle addition of another package of the App ships`.
- **A type that is no bundle, or fewer than two owners — unchanged, right.** `ownersHoldingAName` returns its input.
- **Declared rows, the App arm, the sentinel fall-through — unchanged, right.** The diff touches none of them beyond F2.
- **`overlaySlotBinding` takes `type` as its first parameter — private, right.** All five call sites in the diff pass it. No public export or signature moves.
- **Not derived by the PR — see ④ F4.** Two cases where the new owner count still differs from `packageScopedHoldersOf`.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset level and declaration are unchanged: `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. The delta publishes no new narrowing, so the level holds.
- The one changed changeset sentence matches the tree: "the one package of the App holding the name, counted as the exact read counts holders (a bundle addition ... holds no name, #28802, unless it ships the row's own locale ...); else, with two or more, no package". Both halves are what `ownersHoldingAName` does.
- The FROM → TO lines match the tree. The `getPackageScopedItem` line ("TO the row, when the row declares X or X is the one package of the App holding the name") covers the F1 move through the amended definition. No line was added, and none is owed: against `main` the F1 case is the same move as that line.
- The changeset states the registry's answer for the accepted residual. It does not say the exact read answers differently there. See ④ F5.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Closed: the epic read is on GitHub.** The earlier record escalated that the epic ruling was not on the card. Comment 6814761042 on the PR is the epic seat's red-line read, PASS at `ed0f2baa`. It covers that head, not this one; the lane seat decides whether the delta needs a second read. The accepted residual above is a red-line 2 matter the seat is already reporting.
- No new dev flag and no `open_questions` entry arrived with the delta: the card and the PR hold no comment newer than 6814798935.
- **Escalated to the lane seat: F4's second case** may be off-door data. Whether the save door admits a pair row declaring a package for a locale that package's dependency ships was not read to the end.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, the delta read sentence by sentence against `packageScopedHoldersOf` and `pairRowOnAddress`.

- **F4 — should-fix. `ownersHoldingAName` does not count members the way `packageScopedHoldersOf` does, and two cases still disagree with the exact read.** The jsdoc says "The undeclared arms count the holders the exact read counts". The exact read's set is built over every holder, with each holder's members read through `bundleMembersHeldBy` (composite members plus every bare row bound to it). The new count is built over the pair's owners only, with composite members plus bare rows stamped with the owner's own id. Read in the code, not run:
  - **Case a, an addition to a holder outside the App (errs on the refusing side).** X of App A ships `en-US`. W of another App holds the name. Y of App A depends on W, not on X, and adds `fr-FR`. `packageScopedHoldersOf` drops Y (an addition to W), so `?package=X` sees one owner and serves an undeclared `de-DE` row of `A.custom`. In the registry the owners are X and Y, W is not in the member map, Y is not judged an addition, and the row binds to no package.
  - **Case b, a bound pair row makes the addition a holder (errs on the guessing side).** X ships `en-US`. Y of the same App depends on X and ships `fr-FR`. The pair stores an `en-US` row declaring Y. That row binds to Y, so `bundleMembersHeldBy(Y)` holds `en-US`, Y shares a member with X, and `packageScopedHoldersOf` answers X and Y. An undeclared `de-DE` row is then refused at `?package=X`, naming both. In the registry the count leaves pair rows out, Y reads as an addition, and the `de-DE` row binds to X. The same holds when the `en-US` row sits in an installed legacy pair of Y. The jsdoc gives the reason for leaving pair rows out ("the members a pair row adds are what this answer decides"), but a declared row and a legacy pair's row are decided without this arm.
  
  Case b is the direction red line 2 forbids, if the stored row can exist (③). Fix: build the member map over every composite holder, and count the bare rows whose binding does not go through the undeclared arm. Or declare both cases in the jsdoc and the changeset and pin them. Either earns a delta review.
- **F5 — nit, prose face.** The PR body still describes `ed0f2baa`: 9 cases, +228/−3 over 3 files, and no mention of the addition rule or of the accepted residual. Neither the body nor the changeset says that in the residual `?package=X` serves a row the registry binds to no package, while the body's table row 5 and the changeset title say the registry answers what the exact read serves. Stating it in the PR body moves no head.

**Gate verdicts on this head** (40 check-runs when this record was written): 11 concluded `success`, 16 `skipped`, 13 not concluded. No failure. Concluded green: Check Changeset, Check PR Size, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Dogfood Regression Gate, Test UI, Flag docs affected by code changes, Auto Label, filter. Not concluded: Build Core, Plan Test Core shards (the Test Core shards are not created yet), Live E2E UI, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · ESLint, Lint · CI, release and engine gates, Lint · docs and code guards, Lint · repo and tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus. This verdict is the contract's. It does not cover the runs not concluded, and a red one among them stands on its own as a FAIL of the gate.
